# code-fence-style

- ID: `MD048`
- Category: Code
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `code`

Code fences all use the first fence's character, backtick or tilde.

## Why

One fence character makes code blocks easy to recognize and to search for.

## Options

Set them under `rules.code-fence-style.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `consistent`): Fence character to require.
  consistent takes the fence of the first block. Values: `consistent`,
  `backtick`, `tilde`.

## Fix

The fix rewrites the opening and closing fences with the expected character.
gomdlint reports a block without a fix when the new fence would end it early or
break its info string. gomdlint may report a finding without a fix when the fix
would change a line with one character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or
the lines around it up to a blank line, because it could add or remove a task
list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

````markdown
# Install

```sh
go install github.com/yaklabco/gomdlint/cmd/gomdlint@latest
```

Then check the version:

~~~sh
gomdlint version
~~~
````

gomdlint reports:

```text
9:1 Code fence style 'tilde' does not match expected 'backtick'
```

The fix changes it to:

````markdown
# Install

```sh
go install github.com/yaklabco/gomdlint/cmd/gomdlint@latest
```

Then check the version:

```sh
gomdlint version
```
````

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  code-fence-style:
    options:
      style: consistent
```

Under `rules`, `code-fence-style: false` turns the rule off and
`code-fence-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable code-fence-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line code-fence-style -->
```
